assumptions: Propellant tank is loaded to its full capacity; propellant sizing is not optimised.
Trajectory mission delta-v counts as a spacecraft maneuver only for scenario-preset and manual-estimate trajectories; JPL trajectory figures are informational.
Launch mass limit = the stricter of the mission constraint and the launch vehicle limit.
Each maneuver runs the propulsion load for 1 h (gameplay-estimate).

Power ledger: one representative cycle per phase (cruise, then science = span of the observation plan), each split into sunlit and eclipse parts, with phase-average duty cycles; bus, ADCS, thermal and C&DH loads are always on.
Regulated peak supply per phase = array output + battery capacity x 1C (gameplay-estimate); in eclipse only the battery term applies. The phase with the smallest supply - peak margin is checked.
Battery discharge efficiency = 0.95 (gameplay-estimate).
Average power = sum(P x mission-average duty cycle) over every powered component.
Each measurement is observed by the capable selected instrument with the highest data rate; plan items without a capable instrument generate no data and draw no power.
Link budget per contact at min(planned rate, radio max rate), the rate the ledger uses.
Scenario neo-rendezvous: sun distance 1.3 AU and thermal exposure 'cold' are gameplay-estimate defaults; no eclipse is modelled for the starter scenarios.
Earth range for the link budget is the template reference range 3.74e+10 m (gameplay-estimate).

Power is constant within each phase, so SOC extremes occur at phase boundaries.
Free-space path loss only: FSPL = 20 log10(4 pi d / lambda); no atmosphere, pointing or polarisation loss beyond the explicit losses supplied.
Pr = Pt + Gt + Gr - FSPL - implementation loss - other losses (implementation loss is an explicit loss term); margin = Eb/N0 - required Eb/N0.
Noise N0 = kB x system noise temperature; no interference or coding-gain modelling.
capacity_bps is the highest bit rate with margin >= 0 (not capped by hardware).
PROTOCOL_EFFICIENCY = 0.9 is a gameplay-estimate constant (R13).
Contact rate = min(planned, comms max_data_rate) if link margin at that rate >= 0, else 0.
Contact bits = rate x duration x protocol efficiency x ground availability, never more than the bits available (buffered plus generated so far) at that moment.
Observations generate uniformly over their window (rate x duty x compression); generation and downlink proceed concurrently where windows overlap.
Buffer clamps at capacity; excess is lost and reported as overflow_bits.
margin_fraction = (downlinked - generated) / generated; 0 when nothing is generated.
Required observation time defaults to 1.0 h per measurement when neither the requirement threshold (s or day) nor an explicit mapping gives one (gameplay-estimate).
Capability match is binary: any selected instrument listing the capability counts.

Pointing is binary: ADCS accuracy must be <= the pointing requirement of a matching instrument; the loosest-requirement matching instrument is credited, or only the assigned instrument when the engine assigns one instrument per measurement.
A power shortfall (power_ok false) is a hard zero for all science (gameplay-estimate).
Science score counts RETURNED data: returned fraction = downlinked / generated bits (0 if nothing was generated); collected-but-not-returned data is reported separately.
Mission-level collected/returned fractions are priority-weighted objective coverages.
All costs are illustrative gameplay estimates, not real prices.
Hardware = sum of spacecraft component costs; instrument repeats are counted.
Launch cost = launch-vehicle component cost.
Ground cost = ground-segment cost per mission-year x ops_days / 365.25.
Operations = ops_cost_per_day x ops_days.
Development = development_fraction x hardware.
Reserves = reserve_fraction x (hardware + launch + operations + ground + development).
Low/high bounds are total x low_factor / high_factor (not a statistical interval).
Failure modes and components are treated as statistically independent: R_system = product of component reliabilities.
common-cause failures (shared radiation, thermal, software or power events) are not modelled, so nominal reliability is optimistic.
Failure probabilities are illustrative gameplay estimates from the catalogue.
risk_index is a per-mode mean: sum(probability x severity) / (5 x number of failure modes), range 0..1; adding benign (low-probability) modes dilutes it.
Single-point failure: a component with a severity >= 4 failure mode and no mitigation resolving (by id or tag) to another selected component.
Thermal is a qualitative capability check against the scenario exposure class; no thermal balance or temperature is computed.

Hard gates (status 'fail' => infeasible): launch mass (allocated = wet x (1 + mass margin) must fit the limit), delta-v with reserve, peak power, energy closure, battery reserve, data-buffer overflow, trajectory validity, mandatory science capability, budget, catalogue compatibility, and a downlink where every planned contact has negative link margin.

Warnings (prod 'Watch'): partial link-margin failure, data return below generated x (1 + data margin) or generated data not downlinked, mandatory science not collected or not returned, science below the configured minimum score, thin power/data margins.
mass-margin is a gameplay 'watch' band: warning when 0 <= margin_to_limit < 5% (gameplay-estimate); once the limit is exceeded mass-launch-limit fails and mass-margin is not assessed.
Thermal is qualitative: it is passed through unchanged and is never 'pass'.
Empty or zero inputs (no launch limit, no contacts, no generated data, no consumption, no load and supply, no required measurements) are 'not-modelled', never 'pass'.
Data return compares total downlink capacity (rate x duration x protocol efficiency x availability) with generated data x (1 + data margin), and flags any generated data that is not downlinked.
science-minimum-score is a soft warning; success-probability is 'not-modelled' because it requires robustness/simulation (later phase). Neither is a hard gate.
mission_ready requires feasibility 'feasible': a marginal design (any warning) is not mission-ready.
Suggested actions are rule-based hints, not an optimiser's guarantee.
Weights 30/25/20/15/10 are displayed and sum to 100; total = sum(weight x score / 100).
scientific-return = ScienceAnalysis.coverage_score (returned data, not merely collected).
mission-execution is a design-time proxy; refined by simulation: 100 x mean credit over hard gates (pass 1, warning 0.5, fail 0); not-modelled gates are excluded.
engineering-robustness = mean of clamp(headroom / required headroom, 0, 1) x 100 over the mass, delta-v, energy and data margins that can be evaluated.
resource-stewardship = 100 within budget, falling linearly to 0 at twice the budget; a cheaper design inside the budget scores the same, so cost alone is never rewarded.
operations-quality is a design-time proxy; refined by simulation: 100 x share of planned contacts with non-negative link margin x (0.5 if the buffer overflows).
limitations: Margins are computed from the budget quantities above.

assumptions: Seed 42; event set neo-default-v1.
Experimental what-if run: no.
limitations: deterministic event simulation; not orbital propagation
Launch/deployment lasts 1 d and commissioning 14 d (gameplay defaults, capped to 5 % / 25 % of the time of flight, or of the time before science when there is no transfer).
Approach starts 30 d before arrival (at most half the transfer); mid-course starts halfway through the cruise (gameplay defaults).
Without an interplanetary transfer, cruise (orbit raising / checkout) and mid-course (orbit trim) each last 1 d (gameplay durations).
Science operations span the observation plan; downlink-return runs to the end of the mission.
Telemetry is sampled at phase, maneuver, observation and contact checkpoints from the engineering analysis; it is not a time-stepped subsystem simulation.
Battery state of charge is the end-of-cycle value of the analysis representative power cycle for the phase; the battery is full at launch (gameplay-estimate).
Pointing error is a proxy equal to the ADCS pointing accuracy (gameplay-estimate).
Link margin is reported at contacts only, at the scenario reference Earth range.
Design anomalies fire only where the engineering analysis flags the matching constraint; the only randomness is the day of each declared scenario event, drawn from its own seeded scenario stream.

Event effects are gameplay-estimate approximations: skipped observations and missed contacts are re-analysed by the engine; lost buffer data can no longer be downlinked (downlinked = min(downlinked, generated - lost)); battery dips recover by the next checkpoint.
Plan items are skipped, missed, rescaled or cancelled whole by their start day; an item that starts before an effect window and runs into it is flown in full (approximation).
Propellant effects are telemetry-only: they move the propellant channel (clamped at 0) but do not change the maneuver budget.
All catalogue values are illustrative gameplay-estimate archetypes.

Blackout autonomy is a one-step policy selector over the planned observations (observe with the assigned instrument or hold), scored with gameplay-estimate weights; it is not a POMDP planner or flight software.

assumptions: Propellant tank is loaded to its full capacity; propellant sizing is not optimised.
Trajectory mission delta-v counts as a spacecraft maneuver only for scenario-preset and manual-estimate trajectories; JPL trajectory figures are informational.
Launch mass limit = the stricter of the mission constraint and the launch vehicle limit.
Each maneuver runs the propulsion load for 1 h (gameplay-estimate).

Power ledger: one representative cycle per phase (cruise, then science = span of the observation plan), each split into sunlit and eclipse parts, with phase-average duty cycles; bus, ADCS, thermal and C&DH loads are always on.
Regulated peak supply per phase = array output + battery capacity x 1C (gameplay-estimate); in eclipse only the battery term applies. The phase with the smallest supply - peak margin is checked.
Battery discharge efficiency = 0.95 (gameplay-estimate).
Average power = sum(P x mission-average duty cycle) over every powered component.
Each measurement is observed by the capable selected instrument with the highest data rate; plan items without a capable instrument generate no data and draw no power.
Link budget per contact at min(planned rate, radio max rate), the rate the ledger uses.
Scenario neo-rendezvous: sun distance 1.3 AU and thermal exposure 'cold' are gameplay-estimate defaults; no eclipse is modelled for the starter scenarios.
Earth range for the link budget is the template reference range 3.74e+10 m (gameplay-estimate).
Bus structure mass is included in bus mass and is not added separately.
No generic structure/harness percentage is applied; only catalogue masses are summed.
The ground segment contributes no spacecraft mass.
Allocated mass = (dry + propellant) x (1 + margin fraction).
Instrument quantity equals the number of repeated instrument ids.
Delta-v = Isp x g0 x ln(m0/mf) with physical masses (m0 = dry + propellant, mf = dry).
Only spacecraft maneuvers count toward required delta-v; trajectory-info items are informational and never summed.
Impulsive maneuvers; gravity, drag and steering losses are not modelled.
Margin = available - required - reserve.
Solar flux = 1 AU solar constant / d^2 (gameplay-estimate constant, inverse-square only).
Array generation = P_1AU / d^2 x EPS efficiency x cos(incidence); incidence beyond 90 degrees gives zero generation. No degradation, temperature or shadowing effects.
Average power = sum(P x duty); peak power = sum of P for every load with duty > 0, assuming all such loads run simultaneously (worst case).
Battery starts full. Surplus charges the battery up to capacity with no charge efficiency loss; deficits draw deficit / discharge_efficiency from the battery.
State of charge floor = 1 - usable DoD; the ledger closes only if SOC never drops below it.
Power is constant within each phase, so SOC extremes occur at phase boundaries.
Free-space path loss only: FSPL = 20 log10(4 pi d / lambda); no atmosphere, pointing or polarisation loss beyond the explicit losses supplied.
Pr = Pt + Gt + Gr - FSPL - implementation loss - other losses (implementation loss is an explicit loss term); margin = Eb/N0 - required Eb/N0.
Noise N0 = kB x system noise temperature; no interference or coding-gain modelling.
capacity_bps is the highest bit rate with margin >= 0 (not capped by hardware).
PROTOCOL_EFFICIENCY = 0.9 is a gameplay-estimate constant (R13).
Contact rate = min(planned, comms max_data_rate) if link margin at that rate >= 0, else 0.
Contact bits = rate x duration x protocol efficiency x ground availability, never more than the bits available (buffered plus generated so far) at that moment.
Observations generate uniformly over their window (rate x duty x compression); generation and downlink proceed concurrently where windows overlap.
Buffer clamps at capacity; excess is lost and reported as overflow_bits.
margin_fraction = (downlinked - generated) / generated; 0 when nothing is generated.
Required observation time defaults to 1.0 h per measurement when neither the requirement threshold (s or day) nor an explicit mapping gives one (gameplay-estimate).
Capability match is binary: any selected instrument listing the capability counts.

Pointing is binary: ADCS accuracy must be <= the pointing requirement of a matching instrument; the loosest-requirement matching instrument is credited, or only the assigned instrument when the engine assigns one instrument per measurement.
A power shortfall (power_ok false) is a hard zero for all science (gameplay-estimate).
Science score counts RETURNED data: returned fraction = downlinked / generated bits (0 if nothing was generated); collected-but-not-returned data is reported separately.
Mission-level collected/returned fractions are priority-weighted objective coverages.
All costs are illustrative gameplay estimates, not real prices.
Hardware = sum of spacecraft component costs; instrument repeats are counted.
Launch cost = launch-vehicle component cost.
Ground cost = ground-segment cost per mission-year x ops_days / 365.25.
Operations = ops_cost_per_day x ops_days.
Development = development_fraction x hardware.
Reserves = reserve_fraction x (hardware + launch + operations + ground + development).
Low/high bounds are total x low_factor / high_factor (not a statistical interval).
Failure modes and components are treated as statistically independent: R_system = product of component reliabilities.
common-cause failures (shared radiation, thermal, software or power events) are not modelled, so nominal reliability is optimistic.
Failure probabilities are illustrative gameplay estimates from the catalogue.
risk_index is a per-mode mean: sum(probability x severity) / (5 x number of failure modes), range 0..1; adding benign (low-probability) modes dilutes it.
Single-point failure: a component with a severity >= 4 failure mode and no mitigation resolving (by id or tag) to another selected component.
Thermal is a qualitative capability check against the scenario exposure class; no thermal balance or temperature is computed.

Hard gates (status 'fail' => infeasible): launch mass (allocated = wet x (1 + mass margin) must fit the limit), delta-v with reserve, peak power, energy closure, battery reserve, data-buffer overflow, trajectory validity, mandatory science capability, budget, catalogue compatibility, and a downlink where every planned contact has negative link margin.

Warnings (prod 'Watch'): partial link-margin failure, data return below generated x (1 + data margin) or generated data not downlinked, mandatory science not collected or not returned, science below the configured minimum score, thin power/data margins.
mass-margin is a gameplay 'watch' band: warning when 0 <= margin_to_limit < 5% (gameplay-estimate); once the limit is exceeded mass-launch-limit fails and mass-margin is not assessed.
Thermal is qualitative: it is passed through unchanged and is never 'pass'.
Empty or zero inputs (no launch limit, no contacts, no generated data, no consumption, no load and supply, no required measurements) are 'not-modelled', never 'pass'.
Data return compares total downlink capacity (rate x duration x protocol efficiency x availability) with generated data x (1 + data margin), and flags any generated data that is not downlinked.
science-minimum-score is a soft warning; success-probability is 'not-modelled' because it requires robustness/simulation (later phase). Neither is a hard gate.
mission_ready requires feasibility 'feasible': a marginal design (any warning) is not mission-ready.
Suggested actions are rule-based hints, not an optimiser's guarantee.
Weights 30/25/20/15/10 are displayed and sum to 100; total = sum(weight x score / 100).
scientific-return = ScienceAnalysis.coverage_score (returned data, not merely collected).
mission-execution is a design-time proxy; refined by simulation: 100 x mean credit over hard gates (pass 1, warning 0.5, fail 0); not-modelled gates are excluded.
engineering-robustness = mean of clamp(headroom / required headroom, 0, 1) x 100 over the mass, delta-v, energy and data margins that can be evaluated.
resource-stewardship = 100 within budget, falling linearly to 0 at twice the budget; a cheaper design inside the budget scores the same, so cost alone is never rewarded.
operations-quality is a design-time proxy; refined by simulation: 100 x share of planned contacts with non-negative link margin x (0.5 if the buffer overflows).

assumptions: propulsion-isp (aleatory, normal): Specific impulse varies about 2 % from the catalogue value (gameplay-estimate).
launch-delivered-mass (epistemic, uniform): Delivered mass to the target orbit may be up to 5 % below the nominal limit (gameplay-estimate).
component-mass-growth (epistemic, triangular): Early designs usually grow in mass; up to 15 % growth on every selected part (gameplay-estimate).
solar-array-degradation (aleatory, triangular): Solar arrays lose output with radiation and pointing; 0 to 15 % below nominal (gameplay-estimate).
battery-usable-capacity (epistemic, uniform): Usable battery capacity after ageing is uncertain; 85 to 100 % of nominal (gameplay-estimate).
instrument-duty-cycle (aleatory, triangular): Operators often observe a little more than planned; duty cycle -10 % to +20 % (gameplay-estimate).
antenna-pointing-loss (aleatory, triangular): Antenna efficiency and pointing losses cost 0 to 2 dB of gain (gameplay-estimate).
ground-contact-availability (aleatory, triangular): Ground stations are shared and sometimes unavailable; -20 % to +5 % availability (gameplay-estimate).
Each sample perturbs a copy of the design and the selected catalogue parts, then re-runs the same deterministic engine; nothing else is modelled.
Parameters are sampled independently of each other; one mass-growth factor applies to every selected component in a sample (fully correlated).
Epistemic ranges are sampled as a sensitivity sweep; the result is not a true probability for those parameters.
'Feasible' means no hard constraint failed (warnings still count as feasible).
robustness.disclaimer: Game-level robustness proxy: seeded Monte Carlo over simplified subsystem models. It is not a flight-qualified probabilistic risk assessment, a covariance propagator or chance-constrained optimal control.

Extend the observations or keep the planned schedule? counterfactuals: Plan observation time with margin over each requirement so an illumination surprise does not leave a measurement short.
Schedule observations with slack so a safe-mode pause does not remove a required measurement, and downlink often so little data is exposed in the buffer.
limitations: deterministic event simulation; not orbital propagation
Launch/deployment lasts 1 d and commissioning 14 d (gameplay defaults, capped to 5 % / 25 % of the time of flight, or of the time before science when there is no transfer).
Approach starts 30 d before arrival (at most half the transfer); mid-course starts halfway through the cruise (gameplay defaults).
Without an interplanetary transfer, cruise (orbit raising / checkout) and mid-course (orbit trim) each last 1 d (gameplay durations).
Science operations span the observation plan; downlink-return runs to the end of the mission.
Telemetry is sampled at phase, maneuver, observation and contact checkpoints from the engineering analysis; it is not a time-stepped subsystem simulation.
Battery state of charge is the end-of-cycle value of the analysis representative power cycle for the phase; the battery is full at launch (gameplay-estimate).
Pointing error is a proxy equal to the ADCS pointing accuracy (gameplay-estimate).
Link margin is reported at contacts only, at the scenario reference Earth range.
Design anomalies fire only where the engineering analysis flags the matching constraint; the only randomness is the day of each declared scenario event, drawn from its own seeded scenario stream.

Event effects are gameplay-estimate approximations: skipped observations and missed contacts are re-analysed by the engine; lost buffer data can no longer be downlinked (downlinked = min(downlinked, generated - lost)); battery dips recover by the next checkpoint.
Plan items are skipped, missed, rescaled or cancelled whole by their start day; an item that starts before an effect window and runs into it is flown in full (approximation).
Propellant effects are telemetry-only: they move the propellant channel (clamped at 0) but do not change the maneuver budget.
All catalogue values are illustrative gameplay-estimate archetypes.

Blackout autonomy is a one-step policy selector over the planned observations (observe with the assigned instrument or hold), scored with gameplay-estimate weights; it is not a POMDP planner or flight software.
